messages:
Lauren: Quick sync request — we need to finalize a tiny metrics contract for request/trace propagation so Console can do route rollups and trace drilldowns. Who can own runtime vs infra vs console pieces?

Mike: I can take runtime. Proposed headers: X-Redwood-Req-Id, X-Redwood-Trace-Id, X-Redwood-Sampled (0/1). Generate when client omits. Keep header sizes minimal.

Sanjay: Console needs for rollups: req_id, trace_id, sampled_flag, route, latency_ms, status. For drilldowns: parent_span_id and model_tag are helpful. Req_id shape: 32 hex chars (stable and index-friendly).

Kai: For dashboards minimal ingestion is req_id + route + latency_ms + status. Drilldown panel will join on trace_id to fetch spans. Also want model_variant and fallback_used for rollout views.

Lauren: If a client sends their own request-id header, do we override? Also, can edge proxies be trusted to forward these headers?

Mike: We'll accept client-provided IDs but prefix them in logs with "client:" to avoid collisions. Runtime will NOT overwrite an existing ID. Proxies will forward headers by default; we'll document the forwarding behavior. Also proposing X-Redwood-Sampling-Policy values: probabilistic|adaptive|forced — sampled stays 0/1.

RebeccaK: SRE / billing concern: adding headers increases ingress bytes and may affect quota enforcement. Also enterprise customers may want always-sampled traces — how do we reflect that in billing/ingest caps?

David: We can avoid sending full spans unless sampled. For rollups, emit a compact event from edge when request completes: tiny JSON with req_id, trace_id, route, model, sampled, latency_ms, status, fallback. That keeps trace payloads out of metrics.

Mike: Runtime emits rollup events at completion. If sampled=1 we push full trace to tracing pipeline; if sampled=0 we still preserve trace_id in logs for correlation but don't ship spans.

Lauren: Can someone drop a suggested rollup event example here so Console can prototype parsing? Keep it single-line JSON for the ingest.

David: Example rollup (single line):
`{"req_id":"e3f1a2b3c4d5e6f7890a1b2c3d4e5f6g","trace_id":"t1234abcd5678ef","route":"/v1/generate","model":"redwood-v2-q4","variant":"canary","sampled":"1","latency_ms":"92","status":"200","fallback":"false"}`

Kai: Good. Console wants variant and fallback as typed strings/booleans so aggregations work. We'll add parsing tests.

Sanjay: Sampling defaults proposal: probabilistic at 1% in prod. Adaptive mode ramps up sampling on error or p95 spikes. Need a force-sample mechanism for specific corp customers — propose X-Redwood-Force-Sample with values like "enterprise:<org-id>".

Mike: We'll implement X-Redwood-Force-Sample at the auth edge and validate caller identity before honoring. Also expose server-side config: default_rate, max_rate, adaptive thresholds.

RebeccaK: Action for billing: we should flag forced sampling as a special ingestion class. We need a billing/workload policy so forced enterprise sampling doesn't unexpectedly increase cost to other tenants.

Lauren: Action items — track owners: 
- Mike: implement headers, generator, force-sample hook, doc header behavior (owner)
- David: rollup emitter + size estimate + infra config (owner)
- Kai: Console parsing + dashboard field validation (owner)
- Sanjay: write sampling policy doc + defaults (owner)
- RebeccaK: billing impact analysis (owner)

Mike: ack — will open a PR with header names, semantics, and edge behavior by EOD.

David: ack — adding emitter config to infra repo and example producer.

Kai: ack — will add parsing tests and a mock ingest consumer.

Sanjay: ack — draft policy in docs repo.

ops-bot: :calendar: Meeting scheduled: Propagation + Metrics contract — tomorrow 10:00 AM PT (30m) — invites sent.

Lauren: Thanks all. Please flag blockers in PRs. I'll loop billing in once RebeccaK has numbers."
